chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id from Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Muhammadi al-Alawi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi from Ali ibn al-Abbas from Isma'il ibn Ishaq, all from Abu Rawh Faraj ibn Abi Farwa from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, who said: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to me from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Jihad is a door that Allah opened for His special friends, and He permitted it for them as a favor from Him, and a blessing He reserved for them.
And Jihad is the garment of piety, and the sturdy armor of Allah, and His fortress (1) the secure bond.

So whoever leaves it out of desire for it, Allah will clothe him with the garment of humiliation and the cloak of affliction, and he will depart from comfort, and a seal will be placed upon his heart with similar [seals], and he will be effeminated by smallness and meanness (2), and he will be branded with the mark of depression, and he will be deprived of the half [of his due], and the right will be taken from him due to his neglect of Jihad.
And Allah became angry with him for leaving His support.
And indeed Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said in the clear part of His Book: 'If you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm.' (1)
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly consequences of neglecting Jihad according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates Jihad beyond mere warfare, defining it as the 'garment of piety' and a unique privilege reserved for the *Khasa* (special elite) of Allah's friends. The text emphasizes that neglecting this duty due to worldly attachment results in spiritual humiliation and divine displeasure, while active support for Allah guarantees His steadfast support, a concept rooted in Surah Muhammad.
